flagship.headline: The Beatles reach No. 1 on the Hot 100 with Hello, Goodbye
flagship.summary_line_1: The Beatles' Hello, Goodbye climbed to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 30, 1967, after entering the chart at No. 45 on December 2.
flagship.summary_line_2: The single had come out in November 1967, and the clip below is the song from the band's official Vevo channel.

events.headline: Frank Sinatra records My Way in Hollywood
events.summary_line_1: Frank Sinatra recorded My Way on December 30, 1968, at Western Recorders in Hollywood, with Don Costa arranging, according to the album's Wikipedia entry and the Songfacts calendar.
events.summary_line_2: Reprise released it as a single in March 1969, and the clip below is the song from Sinatra's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles reach No. 1 on the Hot 100 with Hello, Goodbye
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles' Hello, Goodbye climbed to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 30, 1967, after entering the chart at No. 45 on December 2.
events.summary_line_2: The single had come out in November 1967, and the clip below is the song from the band's official Vevo channel.

events.headline: Songwriter and producer Bert Berns dies in New York
events.summary_line_1: Bert Berns, the writer of Twist and Shout, Hang On Sloopy and Piece of My Heart, died of a heart attack on December 30, 1967, according to the Songwriters Hall of Fame.
events.summary_line_2: His version of Piece of My Heart with Erma Franklin was rising on the charts when he died, and the clip below is the Isley Brothers' 1962 recording of Twist and Shout, which he produced, from the group's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones debut on the Hot 100 with She's a Rainbow
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones' She's a Rainbow entered the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 30, 1967 at No. 77.
events.summary_line_2: The song came from the band's album Their Satanic Majesties Request, and the clip below is the track from the ABKCO Vevo channel.

events.headline: Frankie Valli debuts on the Hot 100 with To Give (The Reason I Live)
events.summary_line_1: Frankie Valli's To Give (The Reason I Live) entered the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 30, 1967 at No. 78.
events.summary_line_2: Valli was the lead singer of the 4 Seasons, and the clip below is this solo single from his Topic channel.

events.headline: Strawberry Alarm Clock debut on the Hot 100 with Tomorrow
events.summary_line_1: Strawberry Alarm Clock's Tomorrow entered the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 30, 1967 at No. 80.
events.summary_line_2: The band had topped the Hot 100 earlier in 1967 with Incense and Peppermint, and the clip below is Tomorrow from their Topic channel.

events.headline: Joe Tex reaches his peak with Skinny Legs and All
events.summary_line_1: Joe Tex's Skinny Legs and All rose to its No. 10 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 30, 1967, after entering the chart at No. 93 on October 28.
events.summary_line_2: The clip below is the song from Tex's Topic channel.

events.headline: Donovan reaches his peak with Wear Your Love Like Heaven
events.summary_line_1: Donovan's Wear Your Love Like Heaven rose to its No. 23 peak on the Billboard Hot 100 dated December 30, 1967, after entering the chart at No. 74 on November 25.
events.summary_line_2: The clip below is the song from Donovan's official Vevo channel.

events.headline: The Beatles play the fifth night of Another Beatles Christmas Show
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played two shows at the Hammersmith Odeon in London on December 30, 1964, at 6:15 pm and 8:45 pm, the fifth night of Another Beatles Christmas Show, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: The show mixed comedy sketches with acts from Brian Epstein's roster before a short Beatles set that included Can't Buy Me Love, and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles play the Astoria Theatre in Finsbury Park
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Astoria Theatre in Finsbury Park, London, on December 30, 1963, part of The Beatles Christmas Show, which ran from December 24 to January 11, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Their I Want to Hold Your Hand had been released in the UK on November 29, and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles play the twelfth night of their last Star-Club residency
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Star-Club in Hamburg on December 30, 1962, the twelfth date of their third and final residency there, per the Paul McCartney Project.
events.summary_line_2: Their only single out at the time was Love Me Do, released in the UK on October 5, 1962, and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.

events.headline: The Beatles play an evening show at the Cavern Club
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played an evening show at the Cavern Club in Liverpool on December 30, 1961, per the Paul McCartney Project, two days before their Decca audition on January 1, 1962.
events.summary_line_2: Their only record at the time was My Bonnie, made in Hamburg with Tony Sheridan, and the clip below is that song from the band's Topic channel.
